chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who says: 'If I buy so-and-so, he is free; and if I buy this garment, it is for the poor; and if I marry so-and-so, she is divorced.' He said: 'None of that is anything [valid], for divorce is not valid except for what is possessed, charity is not valid except for what is possessed, and manumission is not valid except for what is possessed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a conditional vow of divorce or charity to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the concept of *milkiyyah* (possession) is applied to conditional vows (*nuudur*), clarifying that the efficacy of divorce, charity, or manumission depends on the actual ownership of the specific subject matter at the time of fulfillment. This ruling prevents the invalidity of vows where the object is not yet acquired, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that legal acts require a valid substrate. The hadith underscores the precision required in Islamic vows, ensuring they are not merely verbal expressions but legally binding commitments contingent on tangible possession.
